spec_match.rationale: The copy and sample now use the current named-trigger grammar and clearly label both columns as illustrations, but standard CSS animations simulate rather than prove AnimationTrigger behavior.

interactive.rationale: Independent restart and no-rewind controls produce a clear repeated-trigger comparison.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index accurately describes the comparison's intended old-versus-new behavior.

edge_cases.rationale: Finished-forward behavior is illustrated; reverse direction, paused state, repeated opposite events, and native trigger state remain absent.

references.rationale: The canonical ChromeStatus feature and CSSWG specification are directly linked.

conformance.rationale: The visible inherited suite exposes the accepted but incorrect view() assertion and does not test the no-auto-rewind runtime contract.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chrome DevTools MCP exercised both controls and finished-state replay at 390×844 and checked the two-column desktop layout at 1280×800, with exact widths and clean console/network.

telemetry_health.rationale: Shared interaction telemetry runs, but no page-specific native behavior assertion exists.

design_system.rationale: Shared variables are used and the comparison now collapses to one column at mobile width.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons and polite live result text expose each comparison state without relying on motion alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The comparison is one column at 390px and two columns at 1280px, without page overflow; all test results remain visible.

openQuestions.title: Replace illustration-only evidence with an additive native use case
openQuestions.detail: Build the ChromeStatus motivation: repeated pointerdown events swell once, pointerup reverses/shrinks, and extra same-direction events do not rewind. Use real triggers where supported and preserve this comparison route as the basic illustration.

guidanceConsulted.query: Expose live feature detection and conformance test results as an accessible educational details interface
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic structure, native controls, concise status announcements, visible focus, and source-linked alternatives for visual state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied native controls, polite result regions, a mobile single-column layout, and the shared visible assertion panel.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Chrome DevTools MCP exercised both controls and observed the live text equivalents at mobile and desktop sizes.

summary: Corrected invalid syntax, browser-age inference, and mobile layout while preserving the stable comparison. Native practical and advanced demos remain open additive work.
